sentences.text: Lady Joan Branson died at the private Lister Hospital in Chelsea A private hospital's failure to provide preventative medication contributed to the death of Lady Joan Branson, an inquest has concluded.
sentences.article_title: Failures 'contributed to' death of Sir Richard Branson's wife

sentences.text: The 80-year-old, who was married to Sir Richard Branson, died on 24 November last year after suffering a cardiac arrest at the private Lister Hospital in Chelsea, west London.
sentences.article_title: Failures 'contributed to' death of Sir Richard Branson's wife

sentences.text: Senior coroner Professor Fiona Wilcox told Westminster Coroner's Court on Wednesday that Lady Joan did not receive prophylactic anticoagulants at the hospital despite a "very high risk of developing deep vein thrombosis".
sentences.article_title: Failures 'contributed to' death of Sir Richard Branson's wife

sentences.text: "I do find her death would have likely been prevented and the lack of anticoagulation did cause or contribute to her death probably," she said.
sentences.article_title: Failures 'contributed to' death of Sir Richard Branson's wife

sentences.text: The coroner's court heard that Lady Joan was admitted to the hospital on 17 November after a fall weeks earlier on Necker Island, a British Virgin Island owned by her billionaire husband.
sentences.article_title: Failures 'contributed to' death of Sir Richard Branson's wife

sentences.text: She died after suffering a pulmonary embolism, a sudden, dangerous blockage in a lung artery, resulting from deep vein thrombosis.
sentences.article_title: Failures 'contributed to' death of Sir Richard Branson's wife

sentences.text: Haematologist Dr George Adams told the inquest that Lady Joan was "extremely high risk" for blood clots and the "biggest risk factor by far was her immobility and her fracture".
sentences.article_title: Failures 'contributed to' death of Sir Richard Branson's wife

sentences.text: From her hospital admission to her death, Glasgow-born Lady Joan did not receive any prophylactic anticoagulation, which is used to stop blood clots from forming.
sentences.article_title: Failures 'contributed to' death of Sir Richard Branson's wife

sentences.text: The hospital's admitting doctor, Dr Basir Kunduzi, did not complete a bleeding risk assessment on the day of her admission, the inquest heard.
sentences.article_title: Failures 'contributed to' death of Sir Richard Branson's wife

sentences.text: Dr Kunduzi said Lady Joan's death led him to "reflect on my role as a doctor" and the importance of "good communication between team members".
sentences.article_title: Failures 'contributed to' death of Sir Richard Branson's wife

sentences.text: Giving her conclusion, Professor Wilcox said it was "not a case of neglect" and there "wasn't an absence of treatment".
sentences.article_title: Failures 'contributed to' death of Sir Richard Branson's wife

sentences.text: After her death, Sir Richard described his wife as the "shining star around which our family's universe has always orbited".
sentences.article_title: Failures 'contributed to' death of Sir Richard Branson's wife

sentences.article_title: Should you sync your workouts to your period?

sentences.text: But she deliberately avoids strict plans because, she says, "there are too many variables at play".
sentences.article_title: Should you sync your workouts to your period?

sentences.text: Some online plans advise women to avoid intense training during their period, she says, yet she has sometimes hit personal records while menstruating.
sentences.article_title: Should you sync your workouts to your period?

sentences.text: "The problem is not that the menstrual cycle is irrelevant," she says, but that "not everything is predictable".
sentences.article_title: Should you sync your workouts to your period?

sentences.text: Dr Faye Bate, a trained medical doctor and women's health expert, is also wary of advice suggesting all women should train differently according to their menstrual phase.
sentences.article_title: Should you sync your workouts to your period?

sentences.text: "A one-size-fits-all model of 'you should be exercising this way in this phase and a different way in a different phase' shouldn't be advice that applies to all women," she says.
sentences.article_title: Should you sync your workouts to your period?

sentences.text: She is concerned that repeatedly telling women they are likely to be weaker or less capable at particular points in their cycle could create a "nocebo" effect - where negative expectations themselves influence how someone feels or performs.
sentences.article_title: Should you sync your workouts to your period?

sentences.text: McNulty tells the BBC that routinely easing off resistance training could also limit progress.
sentences.article_title: Should you sync your workouts to your period?

sentences.text: Strength training is particularly important for women, who face a higher risk of osteoporosis later in life.
sentences.article_title: Should you sync your workouts to your period?

sentences.text: While cycle-syncing itself may not be backed by strong evidence, the experts we spoke to did suggest being "cycle-aware".
sentences.article_title: Should you sync your workouts to your period?

sentences.text: McNulty says tracking your cycle can be a useful way to understand your own patterns, while Dr Bate also encourages women to become more familiar with how they feel at different points in the month.
sentences.article_title: Should you sync your workouts to your period?

sentences.text: Both welcome the fact that menstrual health is being discussed more openly, but say the focus should be on individual experience, rather than rigid, phase-based rules.
sentences.article_title: Should you sync your workouts to your period?

sentences.text: In practice, that might mean having painkillers ready before your period, taking a rest day when symptoms are worse, or easing off a workout if you feel unusually fatigued.
sentences.article_title: Should you sync your workouts to your period?

sentences.text: For Dr Bate, "the most important part is tuning in to how you feel".
sentences.article_title: Should you sync your workouts to your period?

sentences.text: In other words, use your cycle as information rather than a set of rules.
sentences.article_title: Should you sync your workouts to your period?

sentences.text: People will be able to go to their local chemist in England this autumn and get on-the-spot treatment for 12 common conditions without going to their GP first.

sentences.text: Pharmacists can already prescribe medication for seven conditions -  sore throat, earache, sinusitis, shingles, impetigo, infected bites and urinary tract infections.

sentences.text: Five more - migraines, acne, scabies, ear infections and badly blocked noses - are now also being added to that list.
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: For some bosses, it's less about having the perfect CV and more about the way you think, the questions you ask and whether you're prepared to take a chance.

sentences.text: Six business founders and leaders share the qualities they notice most and the advice they would give to people trying to get ahead.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Charlotte Tilbury says one of the biggest things that has driven her career is refusing to let other people set limits on what she can do.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "Nothing is impossible in life - it's only your own limitations you give yourself." The beauty mogul says there will always be naysayers, and there were plenty of people who told her she was "mad" or that her ideas would not work but it's important to ignore them.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Tilbury recommends trying not to think of setbacks as mistakes, but as opportunities to rethink and improve.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "I don't think about mistakes, I think mistakes are opportunities," she says.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Many of the biggest challenges she faced ultimately made her a stronger business leader and "challenge is opportunity and it leads you to greater places".
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Charlie Bowes-Lyon, co-founder of deodorant brand Wild, says attitude matters far more than having the perfect set of skills.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "For me, it's 90% attitude and 10% skills, as skills can be taught, attitude can't." One thing he wishes he had realised earlier is that even successful people do not always feel as confident as they appear and "everyone is faking it until they're making it".
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: If you find yourself at a job interview, Bowes-Lyon says it's really important to have a few questions at the end as "candidates who say they have no questions rarely get the job".
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: One question he recommends asking the interviewer is what success in the job looks like.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Read more about how Charlie Bowes-Lyon runs Wild Marcia Kilgore, the serial entrepreneur behind brands including Beauty Pie and Soap and Glory, says curiosity is one of the main qualities she looks for when hiring.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: She values people who will "roll their sleeves up, ask lots of questions and think about how they can be useful".
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Kilgore also says good communication is crucial as she realised early on in her career that a lack of communication is often the reason things break down.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Her advice to communicate well in the workplace is to "listen to what's being asked and take a breath or five" before responding.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "Your response doesn't have to be immediate, but it does have to be considered." Read more about how Marcia Kilgore built her beauty brands.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Anabel Kindersley, CEO and co-owner of Neal's Yard Remedies, says one of the best ways to build your skills is to keep saying yes to new opportunities.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "Do everything and say yes to everything - it might feel uncomfortable but do it anyway," she says.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: It is an approach that has shaped her own varied career, from working as a child actress to becoming an author and later moving into business.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: She adds that honesty really matters and you should be truthful about your experience and confident in what you can offer.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: When hiring, Kindersley says she looks for people with "equal EQ as IQ", valuing emotional intelligence alongside ability.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Charlie Nunn, group chief executive of Lloyds Banking Group, says curiosity, resilience and an increasing willingness to think about how AI tools can also be used in the future are some of the skills he values most in his employees.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: He also really puts an emphasis on hiring people who are good at working in a team as "at the heart of most jobs is the ability to work together in support of something much bigger".
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: His advice for building experience is to take on opportunities that are outside your comfort zone.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Nunn says he was "terrified" about taking on retail roles earlier in his career, but found they gave him valuable experience.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "If something feels risky, try and do it as you'll learn more from it and it'll build breadth around your CV that you didn't have previously." Read about Charlie Nunn's top ways to manage your money.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: James Reed, chairman and chief executive of recruitment company Reed, says one of the biggest mistakes people make is thinking about what an employer can do for you rather than what you can offer in return.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "The biggest mistake is thinking that the world owes you a living," he says and instead suggests you should ask yourself: "How am I the solution to an employer?" As AI is increasingly used in recruitment, Reed says applicants need to think about how their skills are being picked up by technology as well as by a person.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "Try and mirror the job description with your skills and experiences in your application," he says, so that the match between what an employer is looking for and what you can offer is clear.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: He describes AI as "a wonderful tool", but says it should not replace your own judgement or voice – the aim is for it to strengthen an application rather than expect it to do the work for you.

sentences.text: Spanish intelligence services warned of social media calls for a mass migrant crossing into Ceuta the day before tens of thousands of people entered the territory, newly released government documents show.

sentences.text: Rev Bernard Randall has ended a legal challenge over his dismissal from Trent College A chaplain who used a sermon to tell pupils they did not have to believe in "LGBT stuff" has reached a legal agreement with the school that dismissed him.
sentences.article_title: Chaplain settles LGBT sermon unfair dismissal case

sentences.text: Rev Bernard Randall was sacked by Trent College in Long Eaton, Derbyshire, in 2019, two months after the sermon.
sentences.article_title: Chaplain settles LGBT sermon unfair dismissal case

sentences.text: He appealed and his dismissal , external was overturned, but he was later made redundant after refusing reduced hours.
sentences.article_title: Chaplain settles LGBT sermon unfair dismissal case

sentences.text: After losing an unfair dismissal claim, his case had been set for a new tribunal over possible bias on the panel that made the ruling, and Trent College was ordered to pay Randall about £20,000 in costs, according to a court document.
sentences.article_title: Chaplain settles LGBT sermon unfair dismissal case

sentences.text: Advocacy group Christian Concern said a confidential settlement had since been reached.
sentences.article_title: Chaplain settles LGBT sermon unfair dismissal case

sentences.text: An employment tribunal heard Randall opposed parts of a programme the school was implementing to try to improve LGBT inclusivity.

sentences.text: Randall told the tribunal he believed elements of the programme - devised by charity Educate and Celebrate - were Marxist, revolutionary, atheist and incompatible with Christian values.
sentences.article_title: Chaplain settles LGBT sermon unfair dismissal case

sentences.text: He said some of the terminology within the programme was "ideologically loaded and misleading", and he highlighted phrases such as "sex assigned at birth" and "cisgender".
sentences.article_title: Chaplain settles LGBT sermon unfair dismissal case

sentences.text: He also said, in his sermon : "You do not have to accept the ideas of LGBT activists." sentences.text: Randall was removed from his role as chaplain at the fee-paying boarding school and reported to the government counter-terrorism watchdog Prevent.

sentences.text: Trent College had previously been ordered to pay Randall about £20,000 in costs by a judge At an unfair dismissal hearing in February 2023, the judge said the school's redundancy process was genuine and reasonable, and the referral to Prevent had been justified "from a safeguarding perspective".

sentences.text: The UK needs new regulations for AI products used in the NHS and other healthcare settings, says Britain's industry watchdog.
sentences.article_title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog

sentences.text: The Medicines and Healthcare Products Regulatory Agency (MHRA), which regulates all medical devices and licenses treatment drugs in the UK, has published 44 recommendations to update its policies as the use of AI in the sector rises.
sentences.article_title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog

sentences.text: The technology will soon be routinely used within the NHS, MHRA chief Lawrence Tallon told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog

sentences.text: "What I would expect is that patients will... increasingly see AI as part of the way that normal NHS healthcare is delivered," he said.
sentences.article_title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog

sentences.text: "That should happen in a way that they can maintain their trust and their confidence in what's happening." The report was compiled by an independent commission and involved input from more than 12,000 people including patients and clinicians.
sentences.article_title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog

sentences.text: He added while current guidelines may work for simple AI products trained to spot known symptoms on scans, for example, the rules do not apply to more complex models.
sentences.article_title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog

sentences.text: "Unlike most of the medical products we're used to regulating, these products continue to change after the point of authorization," he said.
sentences.article_title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog

sentences.text: "As new data gets fed in, they learn, they adapt, they drift." And he acknowledged trying to regulate AI is a global challenge.
sentences.article_title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog

sentences.text: "I don't think at this moment in time we can point to a single country, a single regulatory framework, and say that they have absolutely cracked it," he said.

sentences.text: Gareth Davies, who said the scene had looked like one from a "Stephen King film", said his team had used specialist equipment to vacuum up "hundreds of thousands" of cockroaches from the four bedroom property in Pontypridd, south Wales.

sentences.text: The recent warmer weather is thought by some experts to be speeding up cockroaches' breeding cycle.
sentences.article_title: Home with hundreds of thousands of cockroaches like a horror movie, pest controller says

sentences.text: Gareth says cases of cockroach infestations "exploded" in the past year Davies said the shared house in Pontypridd, which had been occupied by student nurses, was "absolutely horrendous".
sentences.article_title: Home with hundreds of thousands of cockroaches like a horror movie, pest controller says

sentences.text: The infestation came to light after neighbouring properties complained about cockroaches, despite residents there never having seen one before.
sentences.article_title: Home with hundreds of thousands of cockroaches like a horror movie, pest controller says

sentences.text: When Davies and his team gained access to the home, they found it was "absolutely alive" with the insects.
sentences.article_title: Home with hundreds of thousands of cockroaches like a horror movie, pest controller says

sentences.article_title: Home with hundreds of thousands of cockroaches like a horror movie, pest controller says

sentences.text: They then treated the property with a high-potency insecticide.
sentences.article_title: Home with hundreds of thousands of cockroaches like a horror movie, pest controller says

sentences.text: Davies said this had caused even more cockroaches to emerge.
sentences.article_title: Home with hundreds of thousands of cockroaches like a horror movie, pest controller says

sentences.text: "By applying the insecticides, that's when they started falling out of conduit pipes, literally coming out of plug sockets, out of the toasters, out of the back of microwave ovens," he said.
sentences.article_title: Home with hundreds of thousands of cockroaches like a horror movie, pest controller says

sentences.text: The treatment process was repeated weekly for five weeks.
sentences.article_title: Home with hundreds of thousands of cockroaches like a horror movie, pest controller says

sentences.text: Davies said further treatments would be needed because the infestation had been so deep-seated.
sentences.article_title: Home with hundreds of thousands of cockroaches like a horror movie, pest controller says

sentences.text: "We've had a massive impact there," he said.
sentences.article_title: Home with hundreds of thousands of cockroaches like a horror movie, pest controller says

sentences.text: "We are picking up now probably 10 to 20 a week in specialist attracting traps, which is to be expected due to the extent of it." He said the property had not been the cleanest his team had encountered, but cockroaches could thrive anywhere there had been a food source, including abandoned food.
sentences.article_title: Home with hundreds of thousands of cockroaches like a horror movie, pest controller says

sentences.text: "How these people weren't ill, I do not know," he said.
sentences.article_title: Home with hundreds of thousands of cockroaches like a horror movie, pest controller says

sentences.text: The cockroaches were identified as German cockroaches, Blattella germanica Davies said the number of cockroach infestations he was dealing with had increased dramatically.
sentences.article_title: Home with hundreds of thousands of cockroaches like a horror movie, pest controller says

sentences.text: "Five years ago, I could count on one hand how many cockroach problems we used to deal with in a 12-month period," he said.
sentences.article_title: Home with hundreds of thousands of cockroaches like a horror movie, pest controller says

sentences.text: "But in the last 12 months, we've had hundreds and hundreds." He said he had already dealt with six cockroach jobs this month.
sentences.article_title: Home with hundreds of thousands of cockroaches like a horror movie, pest controller says

sentences.text: "It's just been an absolute explosion," he said.
sentences.article_title: Home with hundreds of thousands of cockroaches like a horror movie, pest controller says

sentences.article_title: Home with hundreds of thousands of cockroaches like a horror movie, pest controller says

sentences.text: "We've had a lot of weeks exceeding 30 degrees," he said.
sentences.article_title: Home with hundreds of thousands of cockroaches like a horror movie, pest controller says

sentences.text: "Cockroaches thrive in the heat.

sentences.article_title: Home with hundreds of thousands of cockroaches like a horror movie, pest controller says

sentences.article_title: Home with hundreds of thousands of cockroaches like a horror movie, pest controller says

sentences.article_title: Home with hundreds of thousands of cockroaches like a horror movie, pest controller says

sentences.text: Argentine President Javier Milei said that oil companies drilling off the Falklands would face sanctions The Argentine government has said that it will file criminal charges against oil company Navitas Petroleum for operating in seas off the Falkland Islands.
sentences.article_title: Argentina to file criminal case against oil company operating in Falklands

sentences.text: The move came just days after Argentine President Javier Milei said he would  sanction oil companies drilling in the British overseas territory in the south-west Atlantic Ocean.
sentences.article_title: Argentina to file criminal case against oil company operating in Falklands

sentences.text: Reacting to the news, Foreign Office Minister Kirsty McNeill insisted that there could be "no doubt" about the British government's commitment to the Falkland Islanders.
sentences.article_title: Argentina to file criminal case against oil company operating in Falklands

sentences.text: Sovereignty of the archipelago remains disputed between the UK and Argentina more than 40 years after a British military task force ejected Argentine forces which had invaded the territory in 1982.
sentences.article_title: Argentina to file criminal case against oil company operating in Falklands

sentences.text: Speaking in the House of Commons on Tuesday, McNeill said that "the decision by the Falkland Islands government to pursue hydrocarbon production is a commercial decision for them to take alongside the commercial companies involved".
sentences.article_title: Argentina to file criminal case against oil company operating in Falklands

sentences.text: She added that "the future of the Falkland Islands is for Falkland Islanders to determine".
sentences.article_title: Argentina to file criminal case against oil company operating in Falklands

sentences.text: The simmering dispute between Britain and Argentina over the Falklands heated up last week, when Milei said in a speech to the nation that the "winds of change" favoured Argentina's claim to the islands.
sentences.article_title: Argentina to file criminal case against oil company operating in Falklands

sentences.text: Milei has, in the past, been criticised by Argentine veterans of the 1982 conflict for being "too soft" on the Falklands, which Argentines call Las Malvinas.
sentences.article_title: Argentina to file criminal case against oil company operating in Falklands

sentences.text: In his speech on Thursday evening local time, Milei restated his government's position on the territory, saying "the Malvinas are Argentine, historically and legally... there's no debate about that." The president described drilling for oil in the archipelago as a "clear and urgent danger" to Argentine sovereignty.
sentences.article_title: Argentina to file criminal case against oil company operating in Falklands

sentences.text: He also dismissed the result of a 2013 referendum in which 99.8% of the islands' residents voted in favour of the Falklands remaining a British oversees territory.
sentences.article_title: Argentina to file criminal case against oil company operating in Falklands

sentences.text: Milei argued that they were living on land which had been "usurped" by the British and therefore "have no legitimate right to self-determination".
sentences.article_title: Argentina to file criminal case against oil company operating in Falklands

sentences.text: The British government dismissed Milei's speech and stressed that its position on the Falklands was "unwavering".
sentences.article_title: Argentina to file criminal case against oil company operating in Falklands

sentences.text: Hopes that Milei's primetime speech may have been a blip and that he would return to his previous stance of strengthening diplomatic ties with the UK were crushed on Monday, however, when his office announced it would file criminal charges against Navitas Petroleum, several of its subsidiaries and their executives.
sentences.article_title: Argentina to file criminal case against oil company operating in Falklands

sentences.article_title: Argentina to file criminal case against oil company operating in Falklands

sentences.article_title: Argentina to file criminal case against oil company operating in Falklands

sentences.article_title: Argentina to file criminal case against oil company operating in Falklands

sentences.article_title: Argentina to file criminal case against oil company operating in Falklands

sentences.text: There could be tens of thousands more teenagers who are not in education, employment or training (Neet) than official statistics suggest, the children's commissioner for England has warned.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: A report by Dame Rachel de Souza said around 42,000 16- and 17-year-olds in England were officially classed as studying at college, but were not showing up at least half of the time.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: She said they had gone "under the radar" and were "not getting the support that they need".
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: The Department for Education (DfE) said it planned to help colleges track attendance and ultimately to gather that data centrally.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: Unlike schools, further education and sixth form colleges in England are not required to collect or report attendance data.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: Dame Rachel's report is based on attendance data obtained from 262 college groups in England and says rates are "substantially lower" than in schools.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: It suggests that more than half (52.2%) of 16- and 17-year-olds are estimated to be persistently absent by the standards used in schools, meaning they are missing 10% or more of college sessions.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: And around 42,000 (5.9%) are severely absent, meaning they are missing at least half of college sessions.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: The DfE estimates that 57,000 16- and 17-year-olds in England are Neet, and Dame Rachel's report argues that these persistently absent teenagers should be considered as "hidden" Neets alongside them.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: Dame Rachel told the BBC a range of factors led to teenagers missing college, including part-time work and travel costs, and that some had been largely absent from education since the Covid pandemic.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: She said while those juggling part-time employment were likely to miss college every so often, it was those who are "far more vulnerable" who were likely to be severely absent.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: She added that it was "shocking" that the DfE did not collect the data as it meant the issue was "ignored".
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: "It's under the radar and these kids are not getting the support that they need," she said.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: "We have called time and time again for increased investment, better integration of support services and a stronger national strategy for employer engagement," she said.
sentences.article_title: Thousands of teens missing education 'under the radar' of official stats, report warns

sentences.text: Thousands of air passengers have seen their travel plans disrupted after an air traffic control problem grounded nearly 2,000 flights across the UK .
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: When a flight is cancelled or delayed, passengers affected have various rights – such as a refund or be put on another flight.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: However, these can vary depending on which carrier you are flying with and from where.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: Only when an airline is at fault - not issues such as air traffic control problems - is extra compensation payable.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: Here's what it means for you.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: When flights are delayed or cancelled, UK and EU airlines, and other carriers when you are departing a UK or EU airport, have a duty to look after you.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: The reason for the delay or cancellation does not matter.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: So anyone affected by the air transport delays will be eligible.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: That includes providing meals and accommodation, if necessary, and getting you to your destination.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: The airline should organise putting you on an alternative flight, at no extra cost.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: Additional losses, such as unused accommodation, might require a claim to a credit card provider, if that was the payment option used.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: After that, a claim may need to go to your travel insurance provider.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: But there is no standard definition of what is covered.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: It may require a close look at the details of the policy to see what is covered, and in which circumstances.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: Passengers are also being urged to heed travel advice from the UK government , external , as this can also affect travel insurance rights.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: If your flight is covered by UK law, your airline must let you choose between either getting a refund or being booked on to an alternative flight.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: That's regardless of how far in advance the cancellation was made.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: You can get your money back for any part of the ticket you have not used.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: So, if you booked a return flight and the outbound leg is cancelled, you can get the full cost of the return ticket refunded.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: If you still want to travel, your airline must find you an alternative flight.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: If another airline is flying to your destination significantly sooner, or there are other suitable modes of transport, then you have a right to be booked on to that alternative transport instead.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: If your flight was coming into the UK on a non-UK or EU airline, then you should check the terms and conditions of your booking.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: The Civil Aviation Authority advises people to keep receipts and not spend more than necessary.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: Civil Aviation Authority: Delays and cancellations , external You are entitled to the same assistance as for a cancellation if your flight is delayed by more than two hours for a short-haul flight, three hours for a medium-haul, or four hours for a long-haul.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: If you are delayed by more than five hours and no longer want to travel, you can get a full refund.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: ABTA: What are your rights? , external Disruption caused by things like air traffic control issues – but also bad weather, strikes by airport staff, or conflict, or other "extraordinary circumstances" – does not entitle you to extra compensation.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: However, in other circumstances, when it is considered to be the airline's fault, you have a number of rights under UK law , external .
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: These apply as long as you are flying from a UK airport on any airline, arriving at a UK airport on an EU or UK airline, or arriving at an airport in the EU on a UK airline.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: What you are entitled to depends on what caused the cancellation and how much notice you are given.
sentences.article_title: What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?

sentences.text: If your flight is cancelled with less than two weeks' notice, you may be able to claim compensation based on the timings of the alternative flight you are offered.

sentences.text: Travel insurance policies will not usually cover loss of earnings either.

sentences.text: Danielle McQuillan said she does not understand why her son was registered The mum of a six-year-old boy with autism and severe learning disabilities said she has been left "shaking" and "intimidated" after her son was placed on the Child Protection Register (CPR).
sentences.article_title: Mum left 'shaking and intimidated' after son placed on Child Protection Register

sentences.text: Danielle McQuillan said she does not understand why Zac was registered and says she had been seeking more overnight respite care to help her cope with his complex needs and to spend more time with her daughters.
sentences.article_title: Mum left 'shaking and intimidated' after son placed on Child Protection Register

sentences.text: Zac is non-verbal and his mum said his behaviour can be extremely challenging, including stripping off his clothes and running away when they are out.
sentences.article_title: Mum left 'shaking and intimidated' after son placed on Child Protection Register

sentences.text: The South Eastern Health Trust, who placed him on the register, has been contacted for comment.
sentences.article_title: Mum left 'shaking and intimidated' after son placed on Child Protection Register

sentences.text: The CPR is a register of children who have been identified as being at risk of significant harm.
sentences.article_title: Mum left 'shaking and intimidated' after son placed on Child Protection Register

sentences.text: Eamonn McNally, senior lawyer at the Children's Law Centre, said his organisation is increasingly seeing  the CPR used in cases involving children with complex disabilities and additional needs when they are not at risk.
sentences.article_title: Mum left 'shaking and intimidated' after son placed on Child Protection Register

sentences.text: "We have a number of families with significant needs who are under extreme pressure they're at burn out because of a lack of service and support," he said.
sentences.article_title: Mum left 'shaking and intimidated' after son placed on Child Protection Register

sentences.text: "That shouldn't equate to a registration on the child protection register that should equal support being put in place to keep that family together." When a child is placed on the CPR social workers will typically carry out unannounced visits to witness the family in a regular day-to-day setting.
sentences.article_title: Mum left 'shaking and intimidated' after son placed on Child Protection Register

sentences.text: Eamonn McNally is a senior lawyer at the Children's Law Centre McQuillan said these visits can be "intimidating" as she does not know why her son has been placed on the register.
sentences.article_title: Mum left 'shaking and intimidated' after son placed on Child Protection Register

sentences.text: "I've been trying to get some overnight respite as I want to be a mum to my girls as well as Zac," she said.
sentences.article_title: Mum left 'shaking and intimidated' after son placed on Child Protection Register

sentences.text: "I had a disagreement with a social worker about getting a break and they said 'we can't parent your child more than we already do'.
sentences.article_title: Mum left 'shaking and intimidated' after son placed on Child Protection Register

sentences.text: "That really hit a nerve with me as someone who works very hard to be a good parent." McQuillan said the exchange left her feeling "upset and crying".
sentences.article_title: Mum left 'shaking and intimidated' after son placed on Child Protection Register

sentences.text: The next day, she said, two social workers called to her home to inform her that they would be holding a child safeguarding conference with a view to putting Zac on the CPR.
sentences.article_title: Mum left 'shaking and intimidated' after son placed on Child Protection Register

sentences.text: A child safeguarding conference is organised if a child is considered at risk of significant harm.
sentences.article_title: Mum left 'shaking and intimidated' after son placed on Child Protection Register

sentences.text: It usually involves agencies such as social services, medical professionals and schools, meeting with a child's family to share information, identify risks and outline what needs to be done to protect the child, according to the NSPCC , external .
sentences.article_title: Mum left 'shaking and intimidated' after son placed on Child Protection Register

sentences.text: The conference involved 17 health and education professionals, according to McQuillan, with each asked to vote on whether Zac should be registered.
sentences.article_title: Mum left 'shaking and intimidated' after son placed on Child Protection Register

sentences.text: The decision was taken to place him on the register.
sentences.article_title: Mum left 'shaking and intimidated' after son placed on Child Protection Register

sentences.text: McNally from the Children's Law Centre, was McQuillan's representative at the meeting.
sentences.article_title: Mum left 'shaking and intimidated' after son placed on Child Protection Register

sentences.text: The organisation has called for a review of the process, describing it as "out of date and not fit for purpose".
sentences.article_title: Mum left 'shaking and intimidated' after son placed on Child Protection Register

sentences.text: The NSPCC said the CPR allows relevant agencies, such as emergency responders and schools, to check if a child they are working with is known to be at risk.
sentences.article_title: Mum left 'shaking and intimidated' after son placed on Child Protection Register

sentences.text: McQuillan said being placed on the register has increased her anxiety and stress.
sentences.article_title: Mum left 'shaking and intimidated' after son placed on Child Protection Register

sentences.text: "It has meant the social workers have turned up unannounced at my home," she said.
sentences.article_title: Mum left 'shaking and intimidated' after son placed on Child Protection Register

sentences.text: "I just feel like I'm being watched for a reason that I don't know." She said on one occasion she took Zac to McDonald's and returned home to find two social workers parked outside.
sentences.article_title: Mum left 'shaking and intimidated' after son placed on Child Protection Register

sentences.text: "I was shaking, I felt so intimidated," she continued.
sentences.article_title: Mum left 'shaking and intimidated' after son placed on Child Protection Register

sentences.text: I think it's because there isn't a proper reason as to why he's been put on it they're almost trying to find a reason now which is why they're turning up." McNally said families who find themselves on the register can sometimes feel there has been an overreach by social services.
sentences.article_title: Mum left 'shaking and intimidated' after son placed on Child Protection Register

sentences.text: "And what I mean by that is you have people coming into your home checking you out.
sentences.article_title: Mum left 'shaking and intimidated' after son placed on Child Protection Register

sentences.text: "That doesn't actually add anything to the family,  in fact it takes away from the time that they have with their child." sentences.text: Writing a will is probably not on the to-do lists of most 27-year-olds.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: But Erin Atkinson has already decided what should happen to her money and belongings when she dies.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: "At first it felt quite surreal because you associate wills with older people," she says.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: Erin works in psychological research at a London university and moved to the capital from Bristol four years ago.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: She now rents and, although she did not want to share her exact salary, does not see herself as particularly wealthy.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: Even so, she has already decided where some of her things should go.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: Her £7,000 car will go to her sister.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: A gold necklace given to her by her partner will go back to him.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: And she has asked for some of her money to go to a cause that matters deeply to her.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: "One thing that's close to my heart is an endometriosis charity," she says.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: "It felt really empowering that I could have that written down to say I want X amount donated." The 2025 National Wills Report found that just one in five 18 to 24-year-olds has a will in place.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: That rises to 33% of 22 to 34-year-olds, compared with 56% of people aged over 55.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: Erin has left her £7,000 car to her sister and a gold necklace to her partner Writing a will can seem daunting and expensive.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: But there are ways to get one written for free or at a lower cost.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: For example, every November, Will Aid , external works with solicitors who volunteer their time and waive their fee for writing a basic will.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: Members of a trade union may also benefit from a free will writing service, according to Citizens Advice. , external For many young people, making a will may not seem necessary, particularly if they feel they have little to leave behind.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: Sophia Maslin, founder of Morby, a website that allows people to create wills online, says the idea that you need to own a lot before making a will is one of the biggest misconceptions she comes across.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: "People believe they don't own enough.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: But actually, if you've got some sort of savings, investments, pensions, your social media accounts, if you've got pets, even funeral wishes, these are all things to think about," she says.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: For Erin, the idea of making a will first came up when her friend bought a home.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: Then she began seeing Maslin talking about wills on TikTok.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: Maslin had shared the story of her cousin, who died young without a will, and how complicated things became for her family.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: Sophia Maslin created Morby in 2024, inspired by her own family's experience of dealing with wills Seeing her story made Erin think more seriously about making one for herself, while seeing the effect of her own grandmother's will on her family also influenced her.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: "My grandma passed and she had a will and it was very complex because we have quite a large family.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: Seeing the will written in a way that was very directive showed me you can take a lot of pressure off the family," she says.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: The process also made Erin see she had more financial assets than she realised, such as premium bonds.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: Eleanor Hodgson from Crombie Wilkinson Solicitors says there can be practical reasons for making a will even if you don't have that many assets.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: "It's not just your assets that it helps because there's still someone that has to deal with your bank accounts and any debts you have, and it's [being] able to name a person that can legally deal with that without having to jump through hoops," she says.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: Solicitor Eleanor Hodgson says wills can be useful even for people without significant assets The difficulties of not having a will can be hard to appreciate until the time comes, Hodgson adds.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: Maslin says young people can be tempted to put off making a will, assuming it is something they will need later in life.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: "The reality is that unexpected things happen at every stage of life," she says.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: For Erin, some of the things in her will are worth more to her emotionally than financially.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: Her will also sets out some of the smaller details she would like her family to know about, from a poem she wants read at her funeral, to the drink she would like served.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: Thinking about those details did not feel morbid to her.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: "For me, writing a will wasn't about expecting the worst.
sentences.article_title: I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why

sentences.text: The US and Canada have been locked in a bitter conflict since President Donald Trump launched his flagship trade policy on his return to the White House.

sentences.text: The latest escalation has seen tit-for-tat tariffs ramped up to outright bans on imports of certain products, with an easing of tensions looking unlikely anytime soon and further import taxes set to come into force.

sentences.text: Amid all the fierce political rhetoric, people are being impacted by the breakdown in relations between these North American neighbours.
sentences.article_title: What tariffs will really cost Canadians and Americans

sentences.text: Here's what will be affected most on both sides of the border.

sentences.text: If Trump's threat to raise tariffs on Canadian vehicles from 25% to 50% from 1 January 2027 becomes a reality, then that would deal a further blow to the automotive industry.

sentences.article_title: What tariffs will really cost Canadians and Americans

sentences.text: The government is to scrap its advisory body on social mobility, with a new "class unit" charged with improving life opportunities for poorer people.
sentences.article_title: Phillipson sets up 'class unit' as social mobility advisers ditched

sentences.text: The move will see the abolition of the Social Mobility Commission (SMC), responsible for advising ministers on tackling inequality in England.
sentences.article_title: Phillipson sets up 'class unit' as social mobility advisers ditched

sentences.text: Equalities Minister Bridget Phillipson argued the move would bring the government's efforts to tackle disadvantage "in-house".
sentences.article_title: Phillipson sets up 'class unit' as social mobility advisers ditched

sentences.text: But the commission's outgoing chair Alun Francis criticised the decision, adding that class was a "messy concept around which to organise policy".
sentences.article_title: Phillipson sets up 'class unit' as social mobility advisers ditched

sentences.text: Previously known as the Social Mobility and Child Poverty Commission, the body was renamed in 2016 when the Conservative-Liberal Democrat coalition government scrapped legally binding child poverty targets.
sentences.article_title: Phillipson sets up 'class unit' as social mobility advisers ditched

sentences.text: Since then, its remit has been confined to promoting social mobility in England more broadly and publishing an annual report, alongside advising ministers.
sentences.article_title: Phillipson sets up 'class unit' as social mobility advisers ditched

sentences.text: Phillipson said her move to scrap the body, which comes amid wider efforts to cut the number of arm's length bodies in Whitehall, would redirect resources from "oversight to direct delivery" of the government's goals.
sentences.article_title: Phillipson sets up 'class unit' as social mobility advisers ditched

sentences.text: "This decision marks a pivotal step in embedding a focus on socio-economic inequality into the heart of government," she said in a statement.
sentences.article_title: Phillipson sets up 'class unit' as social mobility advisers ditched

sentences.text: Speaking to BBC Radio 5 Live, she said there had been a "squeamishness in talking about class" and it was a "big area that's been missing" in policy formation.
sentences.article_title: Phillipson sets up 'class unit' as social mobility advisers ditched

sentences.text: But Francis, who became the commission's permanent chair in 2023, accused ministers of failing to engage with the body on its plans and said he had seen "no detailed plan" for how the new unit should be assessed.
sentences.article_title: Phillipson sets up 'class unit' as social mobility advisers ditched

sentences.text: In a statement, he added that the name of the unit posed "obvious problems of definition" and "risks being deeply patronising, to equate being working class with being disadvantaged".
sentences.article_title: Phillipson sets up 'class unit' as social mobility advisers ditched

sentences.text: He also took issue with a government press release that said there were no examples since 2016 of its work having directly informed government policy, arguing it had influenced plans for clean energy jobs and the "devolution agenda".
sentences.article_title: Phillipson sets up 'class unit' as social mobility advisers ditched

sentences.text: The government said the new unit would sit within the Office for Equality and Opportunity, alongside existing teams responsible for covering race, sex, LGBT and disability rights contained in anti-discrimination laws.
sentences.article_title: Phillipson sets up 'class unit' as social mobility advisers ditched

sentences.text: It added that the unit would be responsible for introducing a new legal duty for public bodies in England to consider how their policies affect those on low incomes.
sentences.article_title: Phillipson sets up 'class unit' as social mobility advisers ditched

sentences.text: Detailed work on the duty has been ongoing since last year, following a commitment from Labour in its 2024 election manifesto.
sentences.article_title: Phillipson sets up 'class unit' as social mobility advisers ditched

sentences.text: The duty, dubbed "Harman's law" after it was written into the Equality Act by former Labour equalities minister Harriet Harman, was never enacted under the coalition government and has effectively remained dormant in England ever since.
sentences.article_title: Phillipson sets up 'class unit' as social mobility advisers ditched

sentences.text: It has applied in Scotland and Wales since 2018 and 2021 respectively, however, whilst a number of public bodies in England have adopted it voluntarily.
sentences.article_title: Phillipson sets up 'class unit' as social mobility advisers ditched

sentences.text: There is little doubt that the UK's decision to ban imports from Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank is another significant shift in Britain's posture in the Middle East.

sentences.text: The announcement from the Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband , with the Prime Minister Andy Burnham alongside him in the House of Commons, comes almost exactly a year after the UK formally recognised a Palestinian state .

sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham looks to show he will go further than Starmer with West Bank sanctions

sentences.text: This latest announcement is both a logical extension of that decision of 12 months ago, senior figures argue, but also, in words and actions, an expression of Burnham's desire to go further than his predecessor Sir Keir Starmer was willing to.

sentences.text: There is a pride among his team that after a diplomatic effort over the summer, there is a breadth to the coordinated international action on this, with 11 other countries, including France and Canada, sharing the same approach.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham looks to show he will go further than Starmer with West Bank sanctions

sentences.text: "We provided a convening and coordinating role in pulling this together," one source told me, "but we didn't have to convince others to do this.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham looks to show he will go further than Starmer with West Bank sanctions

sentences.text: They were coming to the same view themselves, so we agreed we should all go out and say this at the same time." The hope is that coordinated action increases the likelihood that the measures will have an impact and minimises the blowback to any one country from Israel or America.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham looks to show he will go further than Starmer with West Bank sanctions

sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham looks to show he will go further than Starmer with West Bank sanctions

sentences.text: As for the domestic political context, plenty in the Labour movement and the wider British left have long clamoured for this to happen.

sentences.text: Around 140 Labour MPs went public with this demand at the beginning of the summer, and Burnham was explicit in his criticism of his predecessor's approach to the Middle East, writing in July: "Labour's initial response to the treatment of Gaza caused huge hurt.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham looks to show he will go further than Starmer with West Bank sanctions

sentences.text: We got it wrong and I am sorry about that." In recent years Labour has haemorrhaged support in many communities with a significant Muslim population, and so for a new Labour prime minister seeking to lure as many on the left – and beyond – under Labour's umbrella, this diplomatic intervention makes sense.
sentences.article_title: Chris Mason: Burnham looks to show he will go further than Starmer with West Bank sanctions

sentences.text: Maryam Moshiri is one of the most well-known anchors at BBC News BBC News presenter Maryam Moshiri has revealed she is living with blood cancer.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: Moshiri, who joined the BBC in 2003 and is one of the news channel's best-known anchors, told the BBC she wanted to share her diagnosis to raise awareness about the disease.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: "It's been two years since my diagnosis and I've felt that I've started to understand the disease a lot better and the way it affects my life.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: I've got a handle on it to a degree now, so I felt it was really important to raise awareness," the 49-year-old said.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: "I'm going to have to spend the rest of my life being treated for this," she added.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: Moshiri was diagnosed in November 2024 with polycythaemia vera (PV) - a rare, treatable blood cancer.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: Although it cannot be cured, it can be managed effectively.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: In PV, your body makes too many red blood cells, which makes the blood thicker than normal.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: It leads to a higher risk of developing blood clots, which can cause a stroke, heart attack or deep vein thrombosis (DVT).
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: Symptoms can include headaches, confusion, dizziness and blurred vision.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: "I was told by my consultant that I have this incurable blood cancer," she said.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: "Mostly I had no symptoms and that's one of the problems with this disease.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: "The only reason mine was caught was because my GP was so fastidious in the way she did my routine blood tests and immediately sent them for further diagnosis." As part of her initial treatment, the BBC News chief presenter underwent several "debilitating" hour-long sessions of venesections.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: Venesection is a procedure where a needle is put into a vein in the arm to slowly draw the blood out.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: This blood letting can be an effective way to reduce the thickness of the blood.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: "In about a space of five months, I had venesection seven or eight times.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: So you can imagine my iron levels hit the floor and I felt even more exhausted," she said.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: "After a while I started feeling extremely unwell and tired.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: I started losing my hair, I got itchy all over my body, but the main symptom was fatigue." Later, The World Today presenter was able to get on an immunotherapy treatment called interferon through the NHS, and after some tweaks, she says she is in a better place.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: "I've only needed one venosection in about 15 months, so that's been really good.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: The last couple of months have been better than the last two years," she said.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: "I think it's really important people understand that this blood cancer is incurable but it's manageable with the right treatment and you can lead a relatively healthy life.
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: "It's just a question of finding the right treatment and making sure it works for you." She admits she is "not the person I was two years ago" but says she feels "much better".
sentences.article_title: BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer

sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Not only can cooking in hot weather feel like a chore, but many of us find ourselves feeling less hungry altogether.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So when the heat gets too much, should we consider changing our diet?
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Here are three things to think about next time you're hot and hungry.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking chicken in an air fryer uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven "There's no need for more protein in a heatwave," says Aisling Daly, senior lecturer in nutrition at Oxford Brookes University.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But if you fancy it, some of the most common proteins will need cooking (like meat, chicken and fish) and that can be off-putting in the heat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even an outdoor BBQ can be too hot to handle.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking a chicken leg in the worktop device uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven, according to Radio 4's Sliced Bread .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And because they are smaller and speedier, they also pump less heat into your kitchen.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But experts say don't forget about your slightly less fashionable slow cooker - likely buried in the back of your cupboard.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even though they run for longer, they're typically more energy efficient and release even less heat than the air fryer.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: The reality, though, is that simply by eating and digesting protein, our bodies produce more heat than other food groups.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That's due to the energy needed by the stomach, intestines and liver to break down and absorb these complex molecules.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So that steak you crave will only bring you out in a sweat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But you can also get your protein from lentils, nuts, milk, tofu and cheese too.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: To reduce body heat while still getting your protein fix, Dr Daly recommends focusing on things like bean salads, eggs, pre-cooked meats and plenty of Greek yoghurt (frozen too).
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Making a smoothie by blending up fruit, veg and yogurt (while adding in peanut butter for protein) can provide a balanced, nutritious meal in an easy way.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And it might also be time to turn to some lighter fish, such as tuna, salmon or prawns.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: When it's hot, we lose water when we sweat, so we need to replace it or we become dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Six to eight glasses of fluid a day is normally recommended by the NHS, , external and in a heatwave you could need a lot more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "There is no single amount that suits everyone, because how much fluid your body needs depends on lots of factors like your age, body size, activity levels and health status," says Dr Charlotte Mills, food and nutrition scientist at the University of Reading.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: World Cup footballers aren't the only ones who benefit from hydration breaks: other athletes and pregnant and breastfeeding women are among those who need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But rehydrating doesn't just mean refilling your water bottle every couple of hours.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "We need to eat our water as well as drink it," says Dr Daly, "80-90% of fruit and vegetables are full of water." Cucumber, tomatoes, lettuce, celery, watermelon and strawberries all have very high water content, above 90%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Apples, carrots, cooked broccoli and pears contain 80% to 89% water, as do oranges, grapes and pineapple.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: In comparison, boiled eggs are 75% water , external , with digestive biscuits only 2.8% water , external .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even a cheese and tomato pizza is 38% water, with takeaway chips containing as much as 51%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If your mouth has dried up just reading this, try some of these water-rich recipes .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: A useful way to check if you're hydrated is to check the colour of your urine.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Pale yellow is what you're after.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If it's orangey or dark brown, that's a sign that your kidneys - which filter waste products and produce urine - are holding onto water because there isn't enough in the body.

sentences.text: That means you're dehydrated and need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: After a cold drink, your body sweats more slowly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Your body is trying to keep your core temperature steady at about 37 degrees celsius.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Bear in mind that drinking alcohol also dehydrates.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave
