sentences.text: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem This July, during Britain's record-breaking hot summer, a curious row broke out on X over climate science.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Reform's deputy leader Richard Tice shared a Telegraph article headlined: "Heatwaves caused by fall in pollution." He said cleaner air, rather than carbon dioxide, was behind higher temperatures and claimed the public had been "gaslit".
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: He was wrong to suggest that carbon dioxide is not the primary driver of global warming.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: But the science he was distorting is real - and much more interesting than his original claim.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: The fossil fuels that we've been burning for more than a century produce two very different kinds of pollution.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: As is well known, carbon dioxide warms the Earth.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: But less well-known is sulphur pollution, which forms vast numbers of tiny particles in the air and reflects sunlight back into space, partly counteracting the warming effect of carbon.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Thanks to clean-air policies around the world - like the US's Acid Rain Program in the early 1990s, that reduced gas pollution from power plants - sulphur emissions are falling sharply while carbon dioxide emissions remain near record highs.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Scientists increasingly believe the loss of that cooling effect is slightly speeding up global warming.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: The past three years were the three warmest ever recorded, and the Met Office says 2027 is "very likely" to replace 2024 as the warmest year on record.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: And away from social media, the argument over Tice's tweet raised an even more interesting - and worrying - question.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Is it possible that our planet is actually more sensitive to greenhouse gases than we imagined?
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: And if so, might the climate be changing more rapidly than we feared?
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Global temperatures jump around naturally from year to year.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: El Niño, for example, a natural warming of the Pacific Ocean, can temporarily push them higher.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: So a run of record hot years does not necessarily mean the underlying rate of global warming has increased.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Reto Knutti and his team at ETH Zurich have tried to strip out the effects of El Niño and other natural fluctuations to reveal the underlying trend.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: "It's pretty clear that the rate of warming has accelerated," says Knutti, a professor of climate physics at the Swiss university and a former co-ordinating lead author for the IPCC - the UN-backed body that produces the world's most authoritative assessments of climate science.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: A separate study published this year reached a similar conclusion after accounting for several major natural influences.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: And it seems aerosols are playing a role.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Burning coal and oil releases sulphur dioxide, which forms tiny particles known as sulphate aerosols.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: These particles are bright and reflect some sunlight before it can reach and warm the planet's surface.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Pollution from ships can create bright trails through clouds, visible from space You've probably heard the greenhouse analogy used to explain global warming.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Gases like carbon dioxide make it harder for heat to escape from the Earth, rather like the glass windows of a greenhouse.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Well, sulphur pollution acts a bit like dust on the greenhouse windows.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: The more dust that gathers on those windows, the less sunlight gets inside, and the slower the greenhouse heats up in the first place.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Dr Øivind Hodnebrog, a principal researcher at Cicero, the Norwegian climate research institute, has studied how falling aerosol pollution affects the climate.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: "Sulphate aerosols, they are really small particles, but they are bright particles," he says.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: As well as reflecting sunlight, aerosols also cool the planet by changing the formation of clouds.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Aerosols act like tiny seeds around which water vapour can condense, making some clouds brighter or longer-lived.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Pollution from ships can even create bright trails through marine clouds visible from space.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: So more aerosols mean brighter clouds and more reflection, and so less warming.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Emissions have fallen sharply in Europe, North America and China, while new rules have also reduced sulphur pollution from shipping.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: In our greenhouse analogy, it's as if we've wiped some of the dust away from the windows of the greenhouse, allowing in more sunlight.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: And while carbon dioxide remains in the climate system for centuries, sulphate aerosols survive in the atmosphere for just days or weeks.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: So when sulphur emissions fall, their cooling effect disappears almost immediately.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: The effect is strongest where sulphur pollution has fallen fastest.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: One study estimates it has added around half a degree to summer warming in western-central Europe since 1980.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Prof Piers Forster, a climate scientist at the University of Leeds and another senior author of the IPCC's most recent assessment, estimates that declining aerosol pollution may now be adding around 0.05C to 0.1C of warming per decade.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: But aerosols can only explain part of the recent acceleration in warming.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Greenhouse gases remain much more important.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Forster estimates they are currently adding around 0.2C of warming globally per decade.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: "It is a very significant contribution," he says of the aerosol effect, "but it is not as important as the greenhouse gas contribution by quite a long way." "The aerosols have masked some of the greenhouse gas warming from earlier," is how Hodnebrog explains it.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: "Masked" - that's an interesting word he uses.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: What he means is cleaner air is not causing the underlying warming; it is removing some of the cooling that had been holding that warming back.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: So if cleaner air is only responsible for part of the recent acceleration in global warming, what else is at work?
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: To see what else might be going on, scientists zoom out and look at the Earth as a whole: how much energy it absorbs from the Sun, and how much heat it loses back into space.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Scientists call the difference Earth's energy imbalance.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Cleaner air is part of that picture.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Fewer sulphate particles mean less sunlight is reflected away - in our greenhouse analogy, the windows are cleaner.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: For a long time, the Earth has been absorbing more energy than it loses.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: That surplus is what warms the planet.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: And Knutti says that imbalance has roughly tripled over the past two decades - although the precise increase depends on which years are compared.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Greenhouse gases principally work by making it harder for heat to escape out into space.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: That's what we're all familiar with.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: But when you look at Earth's energy imbalance, you find that there's also more sunlight getting in (and therefore more heat that can be absorbed).
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: So what else might be letting more sunlight in?
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: US President George HW Bush signed a landmark clean-air initiative in 1991 with the Canadian Prime Minister Brian Mulroney, designed to reduce acid rain Much of that change appears to involve something we have already encountered in this story: clouds.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: We saw how sulphur pollution can make some clouds brighter and longer-lived, reflecting more sunlight away.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: But global warming itself can also change clouds.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: As some parts of the ocean warm, low cloud cover can diminish.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: That matters because clouds are bright, while the ocean beneath them is dark.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Remove some cloud and more sunlight reaches the sea, where much of it is absorbed as heat.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: That can create a feedback: warming reduces some cloud cover, which allows more sunlight in, which produces still more warming.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: And the oceans are certainly heating up.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: The World Meteorological Organization says the oceans have warmed more than twice as fast over the past two decades than they did between 1960 and 2005.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Dr Paulo Ceppi, a climate physicist at Imperial College London, says his research suggests this feedback loop between climate change and clouds is more important than sulphur pollution in explaining the recent decline in low clouds.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: But there's still lots of uncertainty.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Scientists say the impacts of cleaner air, natural variations and the effects of warming itself are all tangled together.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: And, when I asked Knutti how much of the cloud change came from each, his answer was simple: "We don't know." And this is where the story takes an even more worrying turn.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: That uncertainty matters because clouds are one of the hardest things to represent in the computer simulations scientists use to project future warming.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Some models show more warming than others for the same amount of greenhouse gas emissions.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Scientists call this variability "climate sensitivity": how much the climate responds to gases like carbon dioxide.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: And the recent observations give Knutti and his colleagues a new way to test those models.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: They found that models which best predicted the recent warming, as well as the rise in the Earth's energy imbalance, are also the ones with a more sensitive climate.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: In other words, the models that predict more warming are looking like the most accurate.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: His team's analysis suggests that the same emissions could produce about 25% more warming than we previously thought.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: We should expect more wildfires - like the ones last year in Los Angeles - if global warming accelerates, scientists say And a study published in the journal Science last year points in a similar direction.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Models which projected relatively little warming struggled most to reproduce the observed rise in Earth's energy imbalance.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Under policies governments currently have in place, the world is estimated to be heading for around 2.8C of warming by the end of the century.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Forster says that if this new evidence proves correct, the same broad emissions path could instead produce warming closer to 3.5C.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: It sounds serious - but there are important reasons for caution.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Warming appears to have accelerated, but Forster says that does not mean it will keep doing so.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: He points out that the recent observations that underpin these estimates cover a relatively short period.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: "We have to be very cautious of how we go about interpreting observations that last for one or two decades," he says.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: The satellite record is short, natural variations are large, and these new studies do not overturn previous estimates.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: But still, some scientists are alarmed.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: So - is cleaning up the air making global warming worse?
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: In one narrow sense, yes.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Removing sulphate pollution takes away some of the cooling that had been counteracting greenhouse warming.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: That really has contributed to the recent acceleration.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: But cleaner air has not caused climate change.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: The aerosol story may help explain part of that acceleration.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: But the wider evidence raises a more worrying possibility: that the climate responds more strongly to greenhouse gases than central estimates have assumed.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: If that's correct, the same emissions could produce more warming than we expected.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Climate risks increase with every fraction of a degree of warming, with the potential for more severe heatwaves, floods, droughts, and wildfires as temperatures rise.

sentences.text: Some of the science we have explored here is complex and important questions remain unresolved.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: But on the central point, the science is clear: the more greenhouse gases we emit, the warmer the planet will become.
sentences.article_title: How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem

sentences.text: Firefighters Matt O'Hare and Shaun Lincoln, from Fordingbridge, were among the first crews on the scene of the New Forest wildfire "It was almost apocalyptic," recalls retained firefighter Matt O'Hare, as he describes the scene that greeted him at the devastating wildfire in the New Forest.

sentences.text: Fans remember former Everton, Leeds and Newcastle midfielder Gary Speed, who took his own life in 2011 Prince William has urged sport at every level to make suicide prevention part of its culture through a new nationwide toolkit.
sentences.article_title: Prince William launches sport mental health toolkit

sentences.text: Launched by the Prince of Wales and the Royal Foundation, On Your Side , external is a set of resources available online that aims "to make suicide prevention as much a part of sport as warm-up, training and performance".
sentences.article_title: Prince William launches sport mental health toolkit

sentences.text: The project is backed by more than 70 organisations including the Football Association, Premier League, Team GB, British Cycling and a host of leading mental health charities.
sentences.article_title: Prince William launches sport mental health toolkit

sentences.text: "Through my work on mental health, I have met people whose lives have been changed forever by suicide," said Prince William.
sentences.article_title: Prince William launches sport mental health toolkit

sentences.text: William added that he hopes On Your Side provides everyone involved in sport who notices someone is struggling the "clear, practical guidance" to help that person find the support they need.
sentences.article_title: Prince William launches sport mental health toolkit

sentences.text: On Your Side is being launched to coincide with World Suicide Prevention Day on 10 September.
sentences.article_title: Prince William launches sport mental health toolkit

sentences.text: William says it has taken 'long time to understand my emotions' According to the Office for National Statistics (ONS), there were 6,190 suicides registered in England and Wales in 2024.
sentences.article_title: Prince William launches sport mental health toolkit

sentences.text: It remains the biggest cause of death for men under the age of 50 and the rate remains notably higher among males (17.6 per 100,000 people) than females (5.7 per 100,000).
sentences.article_title: Prince William launches sport mental health toolkit

sentences.text: A promotional video for On Your Side features England men's football captain Harry Kane, F1 driver George Russell and Women's Rugby World Cup winner Rochelle 'Rocky' Clark.
sentences.article_title: Prince William launches sport mental health toolkit

sentences.text: The toolkit will officially be launched at Everton 's Hill Dickinson Stadium, a venue chosen because its construction included a 'talking bench' in memory of former player Gary Speed.
sentences.article_title: Prince William launches sport mental health toolkit

sentences.text: Ex-Wales captain and manager Speed, who also played for Leeds , Bolton, Newcastle and Sheffield United, took his own life in November 2011.
sentences.article_title: Prince William launches sport mental health toolkit

sentences.text: Premier League record goalscorer and Match of the Day pundit Alan Shearer, who was a close friend of Speed, is among the athletes to have given their backing to the initiative.
sentences.article_title: Prince William launches sport mental health toolkit

sentences.text: "For me, this is obviously very personal," said Shearer.
sentences.article_title: Prince William launches sport mental health toolkit

sentences.text: "We can't always know when somebody is struggling, but we can all be better at asking, listening, and helping someone find the right support.
sentences.article_title: Prince William launches sport mental health toolkit

sentences.text: "You don't have to be an expert.
sentences.article_title: Prince William launches sport mental health toolkit

sentences.text: You don't have to have all the answers, but I hope that everyone in sport will use the toolkit." Prince William said he wants On Your Side to take advantage of sport's "remarkable ability to bring people together".
sentences.article_title: Prince William launches sport mental health toolkit

sentences.text: He added: "In moments of need, the right support can make all the difference.
sentences.article_title: Prince William launches sport mental health toolkit

sentences.text: We all have the power to help, and that's why suicide prevention must be an important part of everyday sporting life." The National Health Service, the Samaritans and mental health charity Mind were all consulted during the creation of On Your Side.
sentences.article_title: Prince William launches sport mental health toolkit

sentences.text: The Royal Foundation said the project had taken two years to complete and added that, although it was being launched to coincide with World Suicide Prevention Day, the initiative is  "not a one-day campaign" and hopes it will have a long-lasting legacy.
sentences.article_title: Prince William launches sport mental health toolkit

sentences.text: Munya Chawawa says he is on "a conscious mission" to use his phone less Comedian, content creator and documentary maker Munya Chawawa became a star in the "golden era" of online video, but says his stage acting debut in Shakespeare is part of a move to "jump ship" from social media.

sentences.text: "I absolutely miss an era where we were dancing for ourselves and not for a digital world somewhere," he says.

sentences.text: Hospitals and healthcare facilities are closing down because of a lack of funding Sudan's fragile health system is on the brink of collapse as global funding cuts have led to the closure of healthcare facilities across the country, Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) has warned.

sentences.text: A simple guide to what is happening in Sudan Sudan's invisible children - born in war with no legal identity "War is driving Sudan's needs; funding cuts are shrinking the response," said Muhammad Ibrahim, the head of charity in Sudan.

sentences.text: "MSF's work in Sudan is privately funded.
sentences.article_title: Sudan's healthcare system on brink of collapse after cuts, medical charity warns

sentences.text: But when funding disappears from other health services, clinics close, patients have fewer places to go, and pressure shifts to the facilities that remain, including ours." This has meant that patients often have to make dangerous and long trips to get treatment.

sentences.text: "After a longer and more expensive journey, patients often arrive in a much more serious condition, and the hospital may already be full," explained Sebastián Traficante, MSF's emergency co-ordinator in the western region of Darfur, which has experienced much of the fighting over the last three years.
sentences.article_title: Sudan's healthcare system on brink of collapse after cuts, medical charity warns

sentences.text: He told the BBC how his family was so poor growing up that his mum would pretend to cook food in a kitchen they shared with others, "to protect our dignity" in front of neighbours.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "I didn't see a way out," he said.

sentences.text: Speaking to John Darvall on BBC Radio Bristol about the publication of his memoir, Etor described growing up in a "compound" with several other families, all sharing a single kitchen, toilet and bathroom.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "It was a very poor neighbourhood.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: To solve the problem, he designed and built a kind of "solar oven".

sentences.text: The Mercator projection is the map widely used across the globe but inaccurately depicts the sizes of countries and continents The UN has just called for the predominant world map to be replaced with one that more accurately reflects the true size of continents such as Africa.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The "Correct the Map" resolution adopted by the General Assembly aims to fix the discrepancy with the Mercator map, in which the African continent is shown as being of similar size to Greenland - even though it is in reality about 14 times larger.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The UN adopted a new map, the Equal Earth projection, which better represents the true sizes of landmasses - but comes with problems of its own.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: There have been many prominent attempts over the years to solve the problem of accurately representing the surface of a sphere on a flat rectangle, each with its own benefits and drawbacks.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Mercator projection has been around since the 16th Century and was vital for navigating the oceans The now widely used Mercator map was created in 1569 by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Its main purpose was to help European sailors navigate the oceans, as cartography Professor James Cheshire at University College London explained.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "He wanted a straight line to be drawn on a map to look like a straight line in reality if you followed a compass bearing," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "That was what it was intended to do, and that's what it does brilliantly well." To keep those angles correct on a flat map, Mercator had to stretch the grid lines wider as they moved away from the equator toward the poles.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: His map accommodates for the curvature of the Earth by making countries near the equator seem much smaller than they are and countries nearer the poles appear stretched.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The distortion is a result of it being impossible to accurately represent the surface of a globe on a two-dimensional chart.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: More than 450 years on, Mercator's creation is still the basis for many of the maps we see in classrooms, on TV and online, including Google Maps.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But critics of the Mercator map say there is a psychological effect to viewing some places as smaller than they actually are and others as larger, as we instinctively view bigger things as more important.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: For Kenyan geographer Kioko Muendo, this has implicitly downplayed Africa's vast resources, population and investment opportunities.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "Maps are more than just guides for travellers - they shape how regions are perceived politically and economically," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Equal Earth map aims to represent landmasses' area more fairly The Equal Earth map aims to address this problem with the Mercator projection.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: It was developed by a team of cartographers in 2018 to present the size and shape of landmasses more accurately, and was inspired by the 1963 Robinson projection - a map that shows the entire globe's surface at once.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: As a result, the Equal Earth map was adopted by African Union members in February, before it was adopted by the UN.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But it sacrifices the straight lines that made the Mercator projection perfect for navigating with - and it cannot be used for measuring the true distance between different places.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "You can preserve area, or you can preserve shape, or you can preserve distance and direction, but not everything at once perfectly, because otherwise you'd be back to a sphere," Cheshire said.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Peters map projection gives a fairer idea of land area but distorts shape The Peters world map was designed by German historian Arno Peters in the early 1970s.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The rectangular map is based on the projection first described by Scottish cartographer James Gall in 1855.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The projection sacrifices accuracy of shape in favour of accuracy of scale.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: So, polar regions are squished, while the bits near the equator are stretched.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This fixes the Greenland-Africa size issue, allowing those who use it to get a sense of the comparative size of different landmasses, all while preserving straight lines of longitude and latitude.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: However, the map severely distorts the shapes of Earth's landmasses, making them all look slightly off.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Russia, for instance, looks much smaller than it actually is.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The straight lines on the Peters map also do not represent true constant compass bearings and so are useless for navigation.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This Mercator projection puts the Americas front and centre instead of Europe and Africa In the same way the apparent size of a landmass can influence its perceived importance, so can its prominence on a map.

sentences.text: Some cartographers have attempted to orient the map so the south is at the top, to counter the psychological bias that comes from the global south being viewed as less imporant because it's lower down.

sentences.text: Letsile Tebogo helped Botswana to 4x400m gold at the World Relays on home soil in Gaborone in May Olympic 200m champion Letsile Tebogo will return to Budapest for the Ultimate Championships next week, but the Hungarian capital is more than just another stop on the athletics calendar for the Botswana sprinter.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: It is the city where the 23-year-old announced himself to the world and where his mother Seratiwa watched him make history for his country by claiming two medals at the 2023 World Championships.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: This time Seratiwa will not be cheering on her son from the stands, having passed away in May 2024 after a short illness.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: Having shared a close relationship with his mother - one she described as being more like a "brother and sister bond" - Tebogo admits that returning without her is difficult.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: "I haven't really looked into the fact that I'm going now to Budapest without my mom," he said.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: "It's just been a bumpy ride having to think about it and having to continue with the grind." Three years ago, Seratiwa surprised her son by travelling to Budapest to watch the then 20-year-old compete in his first senior global championships.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: Tebogo won silver in the 100m and bronze in the 200m - the first World Championship medals claimed by a male athlete from Botswana.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: He also became the first African man to win a World Championship medal in the 100m.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: Seratiwa told BBC Sport Africa at the time that she was "proud" of what her son had achieved.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: For all the memories the city holds, Tebogo says there is also a source of strength in returning to the place where his mother witnessed one of the defining moments of his career.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: "I believe she's always there with me in spirit and in days where giving up is an option," he said.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: A year on from his success at the 2023 World Championships, Tebogo scaled greater heights by becoming Botswana's first Olympic champion when he won the 200m at the Paris 2024 Games, carrying his mother's initials on both his shoes and fingernails as a tribute.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: He returns to Budapest as one of the faces of a new competition created to bring together the sport's best performers.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: The Ultimate Championships is a biennial global event designed to crown the best of the best in a track and field season.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: The three-day end-of-season competition includes Olympic champions, world champions, Diamond League winners and the year's other leading performers.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: The inaugural edition in Budapest, which runs from 11-13 September, has a $10m (£7.41m) prize pot - the highest in track and field history according to organisers World Athletics - with each gold medallist taking home $150,000 (£111,000).
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: Tebogo, who helped Botswana to gold in the 4x400m at the World Relays on home soil earlier this year before registering 200m wins at the Diamond League events in Oslo and Lausanne, says the 200m in Budapest will not only be about looking back.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: He is one of the team captains for the Kids' Athletics Ultimate Challenge, where young people from across the city will be invited to participate in activities at the Gyula Zsivotzky National Athletics Centre the day before the Ultimate Championships begin.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: That will give him the chance to share some of the lessons he has learned since first stepping onto the global stage.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: "I believe firstly you should start with accountability," he said.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: "Think about your preparation, how you want your journey or your season to be, and then also think of unwavering sportsmanship.
sentences.article_title: Tebogo says late mother 'always there' ahead of emotional return to Budapest

sentences.text: "I would love them to have that unwavering sportsmanship, so that they can share lanes, they can cheer for one another." Duplantis releases song for Ultimate Championship

sentences.text: Carlos Queiroz managed at his fifth consecutive World Cup earlier this year, having previously led Iran and Portugal at the finals Carlos Queiroz has been reappointed as head coach of Ghana's men's national team.
sentences.article_title: Queiroz returns as Ghana head coach

sentences.text: The 73-year-old, who had two spells as assistant manager at Manchester United under Sir Alex Ferguson, took charge of the Black Stars in April and led the side to the last 32 at this year's Fifa World Cup, where they were beaten 1-0 by Colombia.
sentences.article_title: Queiroz returns as Ghana head coach

sentences.text: Queiroz appeared to announce his own departure on social media shortly after that defeat, but the Ghana Football Association (GFA) has decided to re-engage him for another spell in charge following internal discussions.
sentences.article_title: Queiroz returns as Ghana head coach

sentences.text: The GFA has not announced the length of his new deal but said he will prepare the team for "a successful new phase on the international stage".
sentences.article_title: Queiroz returns as Ghana head coach

sentences.text: "The GFA believes Queiroz's extensive international experience, technical expertise and knowledge of the Black Stars position him strongly to lead the team into this next chapter," a statement added.
sentences.article_title: Queiroz returns as Ghana head coach

sentences.text: Queiroz has previously led Iran, Portugal and Egypt at major tournaments and has had stints in charge of South Africa, Colombia and Qatar.
sentences.article_title: Queiroz returns as Ghana head coach

sentences.text: Further details on his mandate will be announced by the GFA in due course.
sentences.article_title: Queiroz returns as Ghana head coach

sentences.text: Queiroz said the chance to continue in the role gave him "immense pride and honour".
sentences.article_title: Queiroz returns as Ghana head coach

sentences.text: "Serving Ghana is far more than coaching a football team," he added in a post on Instagram.
sentences.article_title: Queiroz returns as Ghana head coach

sentences.text: "It is a privilege, a responsibility and a mission to honour one of Africa's greatest football nations and its incredible and passionate football people.
sentences.article_title: Queiroz returns as Ghana head coach

sentences.text: "Our ambition is clear: improve every day, unite the nation, make Ghana stronger and fight for every victory with passion, humility and pride.
sentences.article_title: Queiroz returns as Ghana head coach

sentences.text: The mission continues." Queiroz will begin his second spell in charge of the West Africans with qualifiers for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, which begin later this month.
sentences.article_title: Queiroz returns as Ghana head coach

sentences.text: The Black Stars are yet to announce the dates and venues for their first two fixtures in Group C, where they have been drawn alongside Ivory Coast, The Gambia and Somalia.
sentences.article_title: Queiroz returns as Ghana head coach

sentences.text: Lawrence Wong said the pay raise was necessary to attract talent Singapore's government says it will raise the annual salaries of its ministers and other office holders, including its prime minister who is the highest paid political leader in the world.
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million

sentences.text: Lawrence Wong will see an increase of 1.4 million Singapore dollars ($1.1m; £818,000) in his annual pay package.
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million

sentences.text: He has said he will donate this pay increase to charity over the next five years.
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million

sentences.text: Wong said that raising the pay of ministers was necessary to attract better talent.
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million

sentences.text: The government has previously argued that paying ministers high salaries deters corruption.
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million

sentences.text: But the move has attracted criticism in Singapore where there is deep concern about job security and the rising cost of living.
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million

sentences.text: Even before his pay raise kicks in, Wong is still by far the highest paid world leader.
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million

sentences.text: He currently receives an annual salary of S$2.2m and will now see his pay go up by more than 60% to S$3.6m ($2.8m).
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million

sentences.text: Next is Hong Kong chief executive John Lee, who earns about $719,000, followed by Switzerland's president Guy Parmelin with $606,000.
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million

sentences.text: US president Donald Trump earns $400,000 a year, while British PM Andy Burnham takes in $230,000.
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million

sentences.text: On Tuesday, Wong acknowledged that Singapore ministers' salaries have attracted scrutiny given that they were much more than what most citizens earn.
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million

sentences.text: The median monthly income in the country is S$5,775.
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million

sentences.text: But he argued that he has faced difficulty convincing business leaders and top civil servants to run for political office.
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million

sentences.text: While the government cannot match what some of these people earn, "we do not make the financial hurdle unnecessarily high" for them to give up their careers and join politics, he said.
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million

sentences.text: "Overall, I believe this will give me and future prime ministers a better chance of persuading capable Singaporeans to step forward, and of building the strongest possible team for Singapore," he said.
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million

sentences.text: Currently, the base pay package of ministers is about S$1.1m.
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million

sentences.text: With the new pay scheme, that will increase to around S$1.2m.
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million

sentences.text: But Wong said he expects most of these ministers to receive even more than that - around S$1.35m - by the end of the current term of government, as pay will increase based on performance.
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million

sentences.text: Part of their pay package is determined by whether the country reaches certain targets for unemployment rate, income growth, and GDP growth.
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million

sentences.text: The topic of high salaries for Singapore's ministers has long been a lightning rod of criticism for the ruling People's Action Party (PAP), which has led the country since independence.
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million

sentences.text: In a landmark general election in 2011 the PAP saw its lowest vote share in decades, fuelled partly by voters' unhappiness over ministers' pay as well as immigration policies.
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million

sentences.text: The following year, the government slashed ministers' salaries.
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million

sentences.text: Wong's predecessor, Lee Hsien Loong, had also pledged to donate his salary increase to charity for several years back in 2007.
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million

sentences.text: The government has for years pointed to its lack of corruption - Singapore consistently ranks near the top of Transparency International's annual Corruption Perceptions Index - as proof that the ministerial pay system works, arguing that it reduces the temptation for ministers to accept bribes.
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million

sentences.text: But in a country where the average income is far below such sums, the issue continues to rankle and the latest announcement is no exception.
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million

sentences.text: On Tuesday many online posted comments critical of the pay raise, saying it was "tone deaf" given current concerns about retrenchments, jobs for fresh graduates and inflation.
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million

sentences.text: Retrenchments in Singapore hit their highest level in more than five years in the last quarter, according to government figures.
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million

sentences.text: But there were a few who agreed with the move, saying it was necessary to have "the best of the best" running the country.
sentences.article_title: Highest paid world leader to get salary increase of $1 million
